ownership_reason: Only the gold maps an enum value to its formal enum type and reads the JsonProperty annotation of the constant's field there; hops 1-4 pass the values along and place the gold's results (hop 3 one entry per value, hop 1 writing the non-null entries into names). The enum value itself cannot be replaced by a caller: the constant B is the instance of its anonymous subclass however it is obtained, so once the gold has looked for B's field in that subclass and found none, the name 'b' can appear only if a caller re-implements the lookup or replaces the gold. The gold's javadoc promises the name that a JsonProperty annotation on the field of the given enum constant defines; for B, annotated @JsonProperty("b"), the variant returns null. The convention is pinned outside the gold: ClassUtil.findEnumType(Enum) ('enums with "body" are sub-classes of the formal type': the superclass is taken when it is not Enum), used by EnumValues.constructFromName ('Enum types with per-instance sub-classes need special handling') and EnumSerializer; the intact sibling JacksonAnnotationIntrospector.findEnumValue finds the constant's public field through getField, which also searches the formal enum type. testSubclassedEnums (ser and deser: constants with a body through the chain) and testEnumsWithJsonProperty / testEnumsWithJsonPropertyAsKey (annotated constants through the chain) pass.
